Great effort on your Warrior One pose! I can see you're really working hard. Let me help you refine a few key alignment points to make this pose even stronger and more beneficial for you.

First, let's focus on your spine. I notice it's curved right now, but we want to create a beautiful, straight line from your tailbone all the way up through the crown of your head. Try gently engaging your core and imagine someone is gently pulling a string from the top of your head toward the ceiling. This will help you find that strong, straight spine.

Next, let's look at your arms. Right now they're a bit bent, but in Warrior One we want those arms reaching powerfully straight up toward the sky. Think of them as extensions of your strong spine - press your palms together if that feels comfortable, and really stretch those arms long and straight. You should feel energy flowing right through your fingertips.

Finally, let's adjust your front leg. Your knee needs to track directly over your ankle rather than falling inward or pushing too far forward. This protects your knee joint and creates a stable foundation. Try to create a nice 90-degree angle with your front thigh parallel to the floor, making sure that knee stays right above your ankle.

Take your time with these adjustments - there's no rush. Remember, every pose is a practice, and you're doing wonderfully. Let's try it again with these alignment cues in mind. You've got this!
